name: Question 9
problem:
The linear transformation $T$ and the vector $b\in {R}^{4}$ are given below. Determine if there exists a vector $x\in {R}^{4}$ such that $T(x)=b.$
In the affirmative case, find the value of ${x}_{1}-{x}_{3},$ where ${x}_{1},{x}_{2},{x}_{3},{x}_{4}$ are the components of $x.$  

$$
T:[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2} \\ {x}_{3} \\ {x}_{4}\end{aligned}]⟶[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}+2{x}_{2}+{x}_{3}-{x}_{4} \\ -{x}_{2}+2{x}_{3}+{x}_{4} \\ 2{x}_{1}-{x}_{2}+{x}_{3}+{x}_{4} \\ -11{x}_{3}-2{x}_{4}\end{aligned}],\,b=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -2 \\ 3 \\ 5\end{aligned}]
$$
worked_solution:
First, we write down the standard matrix of $T:$

$$
T=[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 1 & -1 \\ 0 & -1 & 2 & 1 \\ 2 & -1 & 1 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & -11 & -2\end{aligned}]
$$

Since $T$ is the standard matix of $T,$ we have $\text{Im}(T)=\text{Col}(T).$ In order to determine whether $b$ lies in $\text{Im}(T),$ we need to check if the equation $Tx=b$ is consistent. 

So, let's find the row echelon form of the augmented matrix $[T\,|\,b]$ as follows: 

$$
\begin{aligned}[T\,|\,b] & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 1 & -1 & 1 \\ 0 & -1 & 2 & 1 & -2 \\ 2 & -1 & 1 & 1 & 3 \\ 0 & 0 & -11 & -2 & 5\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+(-2){R}_{1}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 1 & -1 & 1 \\ 0 & -1 & 2 & 1 & -2 \\ 0 & -5 & -1 & 3 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & -11 & -2 & 5\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+(-5){R}_{1}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 1 & -1 & 1 \\ 0 & -1 & 2 & 1 & -2 \\ 0 & 0 & -11 & -2 & 11 \\ 0 & 0 & -11 & -2 & 5\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{4}:={R}_{4}+(-1){R}_{3}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 1 & -1 & 1 \\ 0 & -1 & 2 & 1 & -2 \\ 0 & 0 & -11 & -2 & 11 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 & -6\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

From the third equation, we get the false statement $0=-6.$ Therefore, the system is inconsistent, and we conclude that  $b\notin \text{Im}(T).$
